name: MO-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+21 partisan lean in a Missouri seat
Incumbent Mark Alford running with a large financial edge
Democrat raised only ~$42k with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's R+21 lean, Alford's incumbency, and his roughly 33-to-1 fundraising advantage over Jordan Herrera leave no credible path for an upset, and prediction markets agree at about 93% Republican. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: A sudden influx of outside spending against Alford or a major scandal would be the only realistic route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark Alford, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second term in Missouri's 4th District, a seat with a strong Republican lean of about 21 points. He has raised nearly $1.4 million and holds over $747,000 in cash, while Democratic challenger Jordan Herrera has raised about $42,000 with minimal cash on hand and no outside support. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any reported fundraising.

Prediction markets give Alford roughly a 93% chance of winning, and no expert raters or public polls flag the race as competitive. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all point the same direction, making this one of the safer Republican holds on the 2024 House map.
